findings.message: The default artifacts have no expire_in; jobs "lint" and "audit" use them.
findings.explanation: Artifacts without expire_in are kept as long as the instance default allows: 30 days on GitLab.com, possibly forever on a self-managed instance. Most job artifacts are only needed by the next stages of the same pipeline.

findings.message: The default image "node:latest" uses the latest tag; jobs "lint" and "audit" use it.
findings.explanation: A floating image changes under the pipeline without any commit: the same commit can pass today and fail tomorrow, and nothing can be rebuilt as it was. `docker buildx imagetools inspect node:<version>` prints the digest.

findings.message: Job "lint" has no rules, only or except, so GitLab's defaults decide where it runs.
findings.explanation: By default a job runs on every branch and every tag. With workflow: rules, or with the project setting that skips branch pipelines for merge requests, it runs in every pipeline instead, merge requests included. Either way it rarely runs only where it is needed.

findings.message: Job "lint" runs 2 times for the same commit: on the default branch and on the tag.
findings.explanation: With merged results pipelines and no direct pushes to the default branch, the merge request pipeline already tests the exact commit that lands on the default branch, and a tag only names that commit. Running the job again there cannot find anything new; it only costs runner time and delays the release.

findings.message: Job "unit" keeps its artifacts with no expire_in.
findings.explanation: Artifacts without expire_in are kept as long as the instance default allows: 30 days on GitLab.com, possibly forever on a self-managed instance. Most job artifacts are only needed by the next stages of the same pipeline.

findings.message: Job "unit" runs in image "golang:1.26", which is pinned by tag but not by digest.
findings.explanation: A tag can be pushed again with other content. A digest pins the exact image, so a rebuild uses the same bytes. `docker buildx imagetools inspect golang:1.26` prints the digest.

findings.message: Job "unit" runs on merge requests but does not set interruptible.
findings.explanation: When a new commit is pushed to a merge request, GitLab can cancel the pipeline of the previous commit, but a job that has started is cancelled only if it is interruptible. This one keeps running for a commit nobody will merge. Setting interruptible: true under default: covers every job at once.

findings.message: !reference [.missing] could not be found; what it stands for is treated as unknown.
findings.explanation: pipewise cannot tell what this part stands for, so the jobs that depend on it are reported as "maybe".
